candidates.attacker_control: Any principal able to create or modify a resource property or a node name in the repository (normal content authors, users of comment/profile style features, or any low-privileged writer in a shared authoring instance) controls strings that this renderer emits. The values come from the resource's ValueMap/JCR properties and path, not from a fixed template.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Metadata is escaped with StringEscapeUtils.escapeHtml (line 107), so escaping is available and deliberately omitted for the other fields; no global OutputEscaping/HttpServletResponse encoding exists in this path; non-existing resources throw ResourceNotFoundException, blocking a purely URL-reflected payload; the sibling PlainTextRendererServlet writes raw values but under text/plain, which is not scriptable, whereas HtmlRendererServlet explicitly sets text/html. No test in the module asserts escaping behavior (bundles/servlets/get has no src/test).
candidates.impact: Stored/reflected cross-site scripting in the Sling application origin: script executes in the browser session of any user who opens the dumped resource, enabling session/credential theft, CSRF-token bypass, and privileged actions if an administrator views attacker-stored content. Scope is limited to content the attacker can write and to users who access the .html dump; no code execution on the server is demonstrated.
candidates.prerequisites: 1) The Sling Default GET Servlet must handle the request: registered for resource type sling/servlet/default, GET, prefix -1, with HTML rendering enabled by default, i.e. any existing resource addressed with extension .html for which no more specific script/servlet is resolved. 2) The attacker must be able to store the payload in a property value or node/path name (write access to that resource). 3) A victim (any user, including an administrator inspecting a node) must request the affected resource's .html dump. Non-existing resources are rejected (DefaultGetServlet.doGet, lines 217-221), so the path itself is not sufficient without an existing resource.
candidates.root_cause: HtmlRendererServlet builds HTML by concatenating repository-controlled data into a PrintWriter without HTML escaping. printResourceInfo() writes r.getPath() (line 105), r.getResourceType() (line 110) and the super type (line 116) raw, and printPropertyValue() writes the property name (line 145) and the property value(s) (lines 147-159) raw, into a response whose content type is text/html (doGet, line 55; enabled by default in DefaultGetServlet, lines 92-93/137-139). The class even imports and uses StringEscapeUtils.escapeHtml for ResourceMetadata (line 107), so escaping is applied inconsistently; no other layer in the chain (DefaultGetServlet.doGet, ServletOutputStream/response writer) escapes these values.
candidates.title: XSS in default GET servlet HTML renderer (HtmlRendererServlet) via unescaped resource path/type/property values
candidates.trace: GET /<path>.html -> SlingServletResolver selects DefaultGetServlet (sling/servlet/default, GET; DefaultGetServlet.java lines 52-64) -> DefaultGetServlet.doGet checks existence, maps extension 'html' to HtmlRendererServlet (lines 223-252, init lines 163-166) -> HtmlRendererServlet.doGet sets text/html (line 55) and obtains the response PrintWriter (line 58) -> printResourceInfo writes r.getPath()/r.getResourceType()/super type raw (lines 103-118) -> render(pw, r, map) iterates properties (lines 120-131) -> printPropertyValue writes name and value raw (lines 143-162). The delivered document is HTML with no escaping of those substrings.
candidates.unverified: Runtime exploitability not executed or confirmed. Exact severity depends on the deployment's authoring model (who can store a property/node name) and on whether a more specific script handles the targeted .html request. The sibling StreamRendererServlet.renderIndex/renderChild (same module, lines 385-457) emits resource path and child names unescaped into text/html as well; this is the same class of defect in the same rendering module but was kept as supporting context, not a second candidate.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

coverage_summary: P1 relation scope: index_status complete, 4,623/4,623 source files indexed, zero missing/mismatched, no SAST/oracle findings loaded and no build or tests executed. I reviewed source text in the API escaping helpers (ResponseUtil/HtmlResponse), servlets/get (DefaultGetServlet + all renderers), servlets/post (redirect/status/handlers), servlets/compat, servlets/resolver structure, engine adapters/error handler, auth core and form (redirect validation, token store, form handler), healthcheck core serializer/servlet, jackrabbit usermanager/accessmanager post servlets, XSS API implementation, and the distribution object-stream filtering; I used the index to trace callers/callees for the main candidate. Large areas were only sampled or not reviewed in depth: most of contrib/ (including experimental modules), tooling/ (IDE, Maven plugins), testing/ and testing mocks, samples/, launching/launchpad internals, scripting engines (JSP/Jasper, Sightly compiler/runtime, JavaScript/Rhino), JCR/webdav/davex/classloader internals, installer, event/discovery internals, and Karaf. Absence of an index record in those areas is not evidence of review.
limitations: No code was executed, no tests or scanners were run; all conclusions are source-reading inferences and no finding is runtime-confirmed.
The P1 index is syntactic navigation only (declarations/calls/containment/file hints); call edges were verified in source text but data-flow and runtime reachability are not proven.

The snapshot is an aggregate of many independently versioned Sling modules (~2017 vintage per launchpad/builder provisioning: servlets.get 2.1.14, healthcheck 1.2.2), so deployment composition (which bundles are actually installed and which auth requirements apply) is not fully determined by this tree.
Only one candidate may be submitted; other plausible but weaker leads are listed as rejected/unconfirmed.
The exact set of writers allowed to store property values/node names in a given deployment determines C1's practical severity and was not verifiable from this source alone.

rejected_leads.lead: HealthCheckExecutorServlet JSONP callback injection (bundles/extensions/healthcheck/core: PARAM_JSONP_CALLBACK -> ResultJsonSerializer.serialize concatenates the request parameter raw into an application/javascript response, lines 233-235/251-264, 66-70).
rejected_leads.reason: Code evidence is clear, but reaching it unauthenticated depends on deployment auth requirements for /system/health (the bundle declares no sling.auth.requirements and the servlet is registered via HttpService); JSONP endpoints are scripting-capable by design, and I could not verify default reachability from source alone. Lower confidence than C1.

The code already rejects URIs with an authority component via java.net.URI (lines 307-321) and appends scheme handling; a possible backslash/encoding normalization bypass is speculative and unproven. The jackrabbit accessmanager/usermanager legacy post servlets lack the same URI check, but impact is low and reachability requires write permissions.

rejected_leads.lead: CQL injection by string concatenation in contrib Cassandra resource provider (e.g. CassandraResourceProvider lines 248, 287; DefaultCassandraMapperImpl line 40).
rejected_leads.reason: Real string concatenation into CQL, but in unsupported/experimental contrib code (static test data, debug prints, not part of default launchpad provisioning), so security impact is not representative of the snapshot's attack surface.

rejected_leads.lead: TokenStore HMAC compared with String.equals (not constant time) and uncaught NumberFormatException/charAt on malformed form-auth cookie (bundles/auth/form TokenStore.isValid, lines 212-259).
rejected_leads.reason: Timing side channel is theoretical over typical networks and the malformed-cookie parse failure is at most a request-level error; neither yields a credible primary finding.

rejected_leads.lead: XXE in urlrewriter rule parsing / SAXParserFactory usages (contrib/extensions/urlrewriter lines 185-199; scripting/jsp ParserUtils).
rejected_leads.reason: Parsed input comes from OSGi configuration (administrator-controlled) or JSP sources (trusted script authors), not from remote attacker input; external entity hardening gaps here do not cross an attacker/trust boundary in default operation.

summary: Targeted defensive review of the Apache Sling aggregate snapshot (4,623 readable files; P1 index reports full syntactic coverage). I focused on the HTTP-facing default code paths (servlets/get, servlets/post, servlets/compat, servlets/resolver, engine adapters, auth core/form, healthcheck, API response helpers) and used the relation index only for navigation, verifying every lead in source text. The strongest source-evidenced issue is a stored/reflected XSS in the default GET servlet's HTML renderer: repository-controlled strings (resource path, resource type, property names and values) are written verbatim into a text/html response, while only the resource metadata is HTML-escaped. No attacker-controlled path to RCE, auth bypass, or SQL/command injection in default-enabled code was verified.
